questions.q: Which of these are facilities an integrated development environment provides? Tick all that apply.
options: An editor for writing source code
A translator so the program can be run
Error diagnostics such as messages and breakpoints
A run-time environment for running the program without leaving the IDE
A guarantee that the program contains no logic errors
correct: An editor for writing source code
A translator so the program can be run
Error diagnostics such as messages and breakpoints
A run-time environment for running the program without leaving the IDE
questions.feedback: Four facilities: editor, translator, diagnostics and run-time environment. No IDE can promise your logic is right.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 1: Tools in one place

questions.q: Match each IDE facility to what it does for the programmer.
pairs: Provides line numbers, indentation and colour-coded keywords while code is typed
Reports the line where a fault was found and lets the program be paused to inspect variables
Runs the program and shows its output inside the same window
Converts the source code so that it can be executed
questions.feedback: Each facility removes a different separate tool the programmer would otherwise need.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 1: Tools in one place

questions.q: State one way the editor in an IDE helps a programmer write correct code.

markPoints.concept: it shows the structure of the code as it is typed, for example by colouring keywords or indenting automatically
markPoints.exemplar: It colours keywords and indents the code automatically, so mistakes show up as they are typed.

questions.example: It colour-codes keywords, numbers the lines and indents blocks automatically, so a missing bracket or a misspelled keyword is visible while the code is being written.
questions.paraphrase: Features such as highlighted keywords, automatic indentation and line numbering make an error obvious as soon as it is typed.
questions.feedback: Anything the editor itself does to make the code's structure visible.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 1: Tools in one place

questions.q: Explain how a breakpoint helps a programmer find a logic error.

markPoints.concept: it pauses the program at a chosen line
markPoints.exemplar: It pauses the program at a line the programmer chooses.

markPoints.concept: so the values held in the variables at that point can be inspected
markPoints.exemplar: This lets the programmer see what the variables hold at that point and compare it with what they expected.

questions.example: A breakpoint pauses execution at a line the programmer chooses, so the program stops part-way instead of running to the end. The programmer can then inspect the values in the variables at that exact point and compare them with what they expected, which is how a logic error is tracked down to a particular line.
questions.paraphrase: It halts the program at a selected point so that the contents of the variables can be examined and checked against what they ought to be.
questions.feedback: Pausing, and what pausing lets you look at.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 1: Tools in one place

questions.q: A program runs without crashing but prints the wrong average. Which IDE facility is most useful here?
options: Error diagnostics such as breakpoints and variable watches
questions.feedback: The program runs, so this is a logic error. Watching the variables change is what finds it.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 1: Tools in one place

questions.q: Explain why an IDE's error message gives a line number as well as a description of the fault.

markPoints.concept: the line number says where to look in the source code
accept: where|the line number|locate|find|position|place|point to|straight to|jump to
markPoints.exemplar: The line number tells the programmer where in the source code to look.

markPoints.concept: so a long program does not have to be read through to find the fault
markPoints.exemplar: This means a long program does not have to be read through from the start to find it.

questions.example: The description says what is wrong and the line number says where, so the programmer can go straight to the fault. Without the line number, finding a missing colon in a program of several hundred lines would mean reading all of them.
questions.paraphrase: Knowing the position as well as the nature of the problem means that the programmer can go directly to it instead of searching through the whole listing.
questions.feedback: Where, and why where saves time.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 4: Diagnostic messages

questions.q: An IDE's error diagnostics will find every logic error in a program.
questions.feedback: Diagnostics find errors the translator or the run-time can detect. A program that runs perfectly and produces the wrong answer looks fine to them.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 4: Diagnostic messages

questions.q: A pupil runs this in an IDE. What does it print?
questions.code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 5):
    total = total + n
print(total)
questions.feedback: range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3 and 4, which add to 10. The IDE's run-time environment shows this in its own output window.
questions.hint: Which values does range(1, 5) actually produce?
questions.revisitLabel: 2.5 Lesson 4 — IDE control room, station 4: Diagnostic messages
